taste.name: Serif speaks the feeling, sans states the fact
taste.trigger: When the page had to address a worried owner and also list concrete tool features
taste.decision: Chose a two-voice system (Stix Two serif at weight 400 for every emotional headline at 56-72px, Dinero Sans 600/700 for every functional label at 14-24px) over the single geometric sans that most accounting-software homepages use at every level
taste.reason: Because an owner who fears bookkeeping reads a book-like serif line ('Clear books. Confident decisions.') as a person reassuring them, and a bold sans line ('Painless payroll') as the tool doing a job; keeping the voices apart tells them which lines are promises and which are features
evidence: Stix Two Text Variable: 17 nodes, all headlines, all weight 400, -1px tracking
weights 600 x72 and 700 x57 live only in sans

taste.name: A new color is a new chapter
taste.trigger: When a ~10,000px homepage (12,200px on mobile) had to carry 11 distinct sections to a non-technical reader
taste.decision: Chose to change the full-bleed background on almost every section (cream, sky, navy, blue grid, cream, sky blue, cream, lilac, navy: 6 hues) over one neutral canvas with cards or divider rules
taste.reason: Because a reader skimming on a phone knows they have reached a new topic from color alone, before reading a word; the bands act as chapter breaks the owner never has to parse
evidence: no horizontal rules between sections in either screenshot
cards: [] in DOM extract; grouping is done by the band, not a container

taste.name: Flat paper, no floating panels
taste.trigger: When the page needed to look trustworthy for money software while already running six saturated band colors
taste.decision: Chose flat surfaces on a warm cream ground (#F9F4F1), two single-layer black shadows in the whole page, and 1px-border 0-radius blog cards over elevated, multi-shadow, glassy cards and gradient hero backgrounds
taste.reason: Because with six bright fills already competing, any depth effect would add a second layer of noise; flat color reads like printed stationery the owner already trusts, and the warm off-white avoids the clinical white of a banking dashboard
evidence: no gradients in either screenshot; texture comes from a flat grid pattern on #0040FF and hand-drawn strokes on the lilac band

taste.name: One ask, one shape, repeated at every depth
taste.trigger: When readers would be ready to start at very different scroll depths
taste.decision: Chose one primary verb in one shape (40px-radius pill, 16px/600, 'Get started now' / 'Get started for free', 5 placements) and demoted every other ask to outline pills or underlined text links, over a menu of competing CTAs such as demo, pricing and video
taste.reason: Because an owner who is not ready yet should never have to choose between buttons; when they are ready, the same filled blue pill is waiting in the band they happen to be in
evidence: buttons: 40px radius x5 primary placements (nav, hero, after proof band, final band, mobile header)
secondary asks: 'Log in' outline pill, 'Learn more about Advisors' text link with arrow, 'Wave vs.' outline tiles
no pricing figures and no demo booking on the homepage
